sections.what-the-student-plays: Five nights of set-one-number-and-wait: a facts card, one big price dial anchored at the season-plan price ($24 of a $10-$120 range), a secondary event-spend stepper, a Night-4 upper-bowl toggle, and one dominant LOCK IT IN button behind a confirm guard. No pre-lock preview of any kind, confirmed absent on every night's screen ('No preview. Nothing on this screen tells you what tonight will make.'). Two non-summable books (CASH, RENEWALS) update in a compact header strip after each close. REVEAL/ADAPT/COUNTERFACTUAL/SYNTHESIS move to the class board with a stronger, more premium visual register (arena backdrop, one chart per frame, one punchline sentence) than the student's own device carries.
sections.biggest-failure: The just-closed night's result is buried below the fold behind the NEXT night's full pricing UI on the 1366x768 student viewport. Confirmed at Night1->2 (screens-kid-b/06-play-night1-RESULT.png viewport vs -FULL.png fullPage: 0 attendance / -$520,000 result card sits ~700px below the fold, hidden behind Night 2's fresh dial and its own LOCK IT IN button) and again at Night2->3 (09-play-night2-RESULT-FULL.png: a sellout with 1,208 turned away, likewise buried). This inverts the founder-preserved reference decision that 'the result is a separate, larger state than the decision' (VISUAL_REFERENCE_SPEC section 2). For a persona who reads little and acts on the first big number/button she sees, the experience->consequence->adaptation loop that is this lesson's entire spine can be played end to end without the student ever reading a single per-night result card on her own screen -- only the compact red/gold CASH and RENEWALS header numbers are guaranteed visible, which register as 'good/bad' but not 'why.'
sections.moment-by-moment-notes: Join flow is clean, one screen, one CTA. HOOK is ~259 words and Night 1's pre-lock screen adds ~170 more before the first LOCK IT IN (measured on raw text dumps) -- heavy for this persona, though the hero price figure and dial and CTA remain findable without reading, so the mechanic itself is operable. The recurring blue guidance paragraph explaining the season-plan anchor repeats verbatim every night; a skim-first reader who reads it once (or never) then habituates to skipping it, so the actual pricing rule is experienced as an unexplained pattern rather than a taught mechanic. Kid B's naive play (price near dial max Night 1 -> zero attendance -> overcorrect near dial floor Night 2 -> sellout with fans turned away -> repeat Night 1's exact price on Night 5, same card, same result: zero again) produced a real, attributable, replayable causal story -- but that story lived in result cards the persona would structurally miss per the biggest-failure above. The Night-4 bowl toggle (CLOSED/OPEN, $95,000 cost) is legible and operable without reading its caption -- a genuine strength. The end-of-PLAY five-row summary table (17-play-night5-RESULT-allnights.png) is the one screen in the whole PLAY phase a fast reader could parse in ten seconds and should be the template for every per-night result, not just the final one. Board frames in REVEAL/ADAPT/COUNTERFACTUAL/SYNTHESIS are visually strong and would likely carry this persona's engagement if she is watching the class screen, independent of her own device's flaws. This was a solo one-desk test session; the COUNTERFACTUAL 'did anybody charge less and make more' prompt has no positive cross-desk answer at n=1 -- NOT VERIFIED as a flaw at real class scale.
sections.required-repairs: (1) Reorder or resequence the per-night transition so the just-closed night's result renders as its own screen state fully inside the 1366x768 viewport before the next night's pricing dial and LOCK button become the dominant on-screen action -- currently the next decision sits above the previous consequence in scroll order, screens-kid-b/06-play-night1-RESULT.png vs -FULL.png. (2) Stop repeating the identical guidance paragraph verbatim every night; either compress after Night 1 or make it reference the student's own last result so a skim-first reader gets a second real chance to absorb the mechanic. (3) Use the end-of-play summary table's glanceable table format (17-play-night5-RESULT-allnights.png) as the design template for every individual night's result card, not only the final one. Not recommending changes to: the join flow, the single-hero-figure-plus-single-CTA pricing card structure, the blind-commitment discipline (verified absent preview on every pre-lock screen), the bowl toggle's legible state change, or the board's visual register in REVEAL/ADAPT/COUNTERFACTUAL/SYNTHESIS.

data.finding: For the casual/low-reading grade 5-6 student pairs-on-one-device persona, the current M2L1 Full House build should not ship to a real classroom as-is. Every per-night result card renders below the fold behind the next night's full pricing UI on a 1366x768 student viewport (confirmed at two consecutive night transitions), inverting the founder's own preserved reference decision that the consequence gets a separate, larger screen state than the decision. A fast, low-reading student can play all five nights end to end -- dial, LOCK IT IN, dial, LOCK IT IN -- without ever reading a single one of her own result cards, leaving the experience->consequence->adaptation loop that is this lesson's core promise dependent entirely on a compact header number and, later, the class board -- not on anything her own device reliably shows her at the moment it matters.

sections.what-the-student-plays: SIMULATED KID / AGENT-PLAYTESTED. Full pass of M2L1 Full House on the real build (port 4405) as a grade 5-6 student who follows no sport, /play at 1366x768, board at 1920x1080, five nights + reveal + adapt + counterfactual + synthesis. What the kid plays: a blind price commitment on a real dial ($10-$120), a subordinate event-spend stepper, and a one-night upper-bowl option, against a printed card (day, visiting club, Draw x/100, TV) and a two-book scoreboard (CASH, RENEWALS) that cannot be summed. Chosen line: N1 $20 / N2 $30+$10k / N3 $40+$20k / N4 $38+$20k+bowl (sold out 22,200, 2,150 turned away) / N5 $28, ending $1,615,864 and 54%. The decision is genuine and blind (OBSERVED: 'No preview. Nothing on this screen tells you what tonight will make.'), the consequence is attributable, and the Night-3 turnout collapse and Night-4 sellout are real surprises. The game is fully playable with zero sports knowledge: every card carries a Draw number, a five-dot meter and at least one plain-English line naming the economic force.
sections.pull-rating: FUNCTIONAL for this persona — below the Track 101 bar for a module finale. Not WEAK: the mechanic is real, the constraint bites, two moments genuinely surprised, and the kid finished wanting one more round with a specific plan (hold near $30 on small nights and watch renewals). Not STRONG: the payoff of every loop renders below the fold on the design-target viewport, the surface is a ~610px text column inside a 1366px screen, the building the kid is supposedly running is never drawn (a 6px bar), turnout and renewal changes arrive with no reason line, and the kid's own desk is never named in front of the room.
sections.biggest-failure: OBSERVED — the consequence is below the fold and underneath the next decision. At 1366x768 each new night loads as card + dials + LOCK IT IN, with last night's result filed beneath the next choice; KEPT and the renewals change sit ~120-140px past the fold on Night 2 (kid-c-fold-viewport vs kid-c-fold-fullpage), the Night-3 collapse is entirely below it by Night 4, and the single theatrical beat in the whole student surface — FULL HOUSE / 22,200 of 22,200 / 2,150 could not get in — renders at y~760-890 (kid-c-sellout). The price dial also re-arms at the plan price $24 every night, so the screen is ready to take a click before the kid has been shown anything. For a student with no sports intuition, watching what happened last time is the only learning channel there is, and the layout hides it.
sections.moment-by-moment-notes: LOBBY: the rejoin PIN is the largest element on first contact; team identity is text only, but 'The biggest market in American sports. A lot of people, and a lot of them can pay.' is a working non-fan cue. HOOK: ~90 words of prose before any number; 'roster' in sentence one and 'season ticket / season plan / renewals' used throughout and never defined; the five-night slate with Draw numbers is behind a collapsed disclosure that sits below the fold (VERIFIED it stays open once clicked). PLAY N1: dial understood in seconds; the event-spend dial ('up to $120,000') has no visible purpose until a 100-word disclosure is opened; the knob overlaps the PLAN $24 label (kid-c-n1-decision). Locked-waiting is one sentence plus ~450px of black. N2-N3: results readable and arithmetic is plain (CAME x PRICE = TICKET MONEY), but each new night pushes the previous result further under the fold. N3 surprise: $40 on the biggest card so far drew only 68.2% and cash fell — no sentence on the result panel says why; the reason lives in a blue rule box further up. N4: card says demand will run past the building; sellout + 2,150 turned away + the honest 'last night's $20,000 bought nothing' verdict are the strongest writing in the product and both are below the fold (kid-c-sellout). N5: 'The only thing that has changed since Night 1 is you' lands. REVEAL: seven stages of the same scatter accumulating shapes, opening with 'this picture is NOT a demand curve' — a term not yet taught — and by stage 4 carrying a 6-line WNBA paragraph over a shrunken chart (kid-c-board-shock); no desk is named in any reveal stage, so the kid never sees their own five nights in front of the class. THE TWO PEAKS frame ('The cheaper ticket made more money') is clear and needs no sports knowledge. ADAPT: three numbered questions on a card — the worksheet moment (kid-c-adapt-worksheet); Q1 asks about a 'best price' the kid was never given. sections.what-the-student-plays: SIMULATED KID / AGENT-PLAYTESTED. Kid A (grade 5-6 NBA obsessive, Desk 1 New York Knicks, pairs on one 1366x768 device) played one full pass of M2L1 Full House on port 4403: LOBBY, HOOK, five nights, REVEAL x7, ADAPT, COUNTERFACTUAL, SYNTHESIS x6, COMPLETE, with 4 desks, a live teacher and a live projector. The mechanic: read a printed night card (day, visiting club's Draw 0-100, TV), drag one price slider between $10 and $120, optionally step a second unlabelled money dial, on Night 4 toggle an upper-bowl option, press LOCK IT IN, wait for the teacher's bell, repeat five times, then watch a teacher-paced board reveal. Kid A's line: $34 / $44 / $60 + $60,000 event money / $90 + bowl open / $34 on Night 1's repeated card. Ended $1,928,456 cash and 0% renewals. The blind commitment is real and produced genuine argument; the second dial was abandoned after the game's own copy said it is 'small either way, next to what your price does'. Two moments genuinely surprised: 7,810 people (39.4%) on the big-name Night 3, and 800 fewer people on Night 5 at the identical price. Both landed offscreen.

data.finding: M2L1 Full House should not ship to a real grades 5-6 class as-is for the sports-fluent student. At the classroom's own 1366x768 viewport the night result renders at top=758px and the box score at top=813px with scrollY=0 and no auto-scroll, so the consequence of the pair's own decision is offscreen after every bell; the lesson's title event, the sellout, is cut off by the bottom of the screen; at 1024x600 the LOCK IT IN control itself is below the fold. Across the seven-stage teacher-paced reveal the student device is byte-identical in all eight captured frames (md5 05aa7a5185a8c10e1dcbde46ce5b736f) and already displays THE TWO PEAKS at stage 0, while the board still reads 'waiting for your teacher' - the lesson's punchline reaches every desk six stages before the room. Renewals fall 50% to 0% with no alarm state and no per-night explanation, and the printed renewals rule mispredicts the student's own largest result. The economics underneath is alive and worth keeping; the surface, staging and pacing currently prevent a real classroom from experiencing it. SIMULATED KID / AGENT-PLAYTESTED - not human-tested.

sections.direction: Ranked by grade movement per unit of work; 1-3 are most of the distance. (1) Rebuild /teach as a fixed monitor wall - persistent header, persistent bottom control bar (advance/bell/reveal/Two Peaks), desk grid in the middle, director rail scrolling inside itself; nothing a teacher touches during a night may be below the fold at 1366x768; fix the tile text wrap in the same pass. (2) Give the settled night its own state on /play above the fold, and make that the place the drawn arena earns itself (fill-encoded bowl, whole-bowl sellout, one edge flash); this also gives the dead locked-waiting screen something to be. (3) One hero per state on all three surfaces - price >=64px on /play with the PIN never larger, one 72-96px figure per board frame, standing caveats demoted to a fixed small footnote rail, #hud off the projector. (4) Give the six synthesis cards computed visuals using the class's own numbers, and move the source notes off the final frame. (5) Then introduce the reference's card grid into /play's 750px of unused width - after (2), so it is designed around the decision/consequence split rather than retro-fitted. (6) Then the craft pass: tick/knob overprint, bar-chip collisions, chart frames and mark rings and the invisible legend swatch, backdrop overprint, 11px muted copy, and the motion vocabulary inside the existing reduced-motion collapse. Reference conflicts needing a founder ruling BEFORE the grid work, because they touch the shared theme that Module 1 also renders: violet-only accent with no gold (conflicts with VISUAL_IDENTITY's accent-gold = money and would make M1 and M2 look like two products), and 'no condensed display face on student/teacher' (conflicts with Bebas Neue eyebrows now in use). Fifteen reference decisions that would cause concrete problems if implemented literally are enumerated in the report's reference-conflicts section - six confirm the spec's own PRELIMINARY flags (pre-lock revenue preview, single 'maximize revenue' goal, the target-price pill, the trophy/momentum footer, vs-projected deltas, a single 'profit' column), nine are additional, including: a student-side history curve with a live current-price marker is still a demand preview; green-for-positive on both books invites the summing the lesson forbids; a 220px sidebar costs the 1024x600 decision column it cannot afford; a per-desk 'Readiness' score is a rank a teacher will read aloud; a paginated /teach desk grid removes the surface's whole purpose; and the projector table must be designed at 1366x768 with 15 desks first, not compressed afterwards. Ten currently-good things must not regress - listed in the report's do-not-regress section, led by the on-screen declaration of blind commitment, the two books never being summed on any surface, projector privacy, the market-colour/night-shape mark system with no joining stroke, the Two Peaks choreography, and the box-score equation.

sections.mechanism-verdicts: STRUCTURAL FINDING FIRST: Full House registers NO ClaimAtom and NO test in this repo reads a line of runtime/src/client/**. ClaimAtom/Claimed/ClaimSurface and the COVERAGE/VALUE/QUANTIFIER/LEVEL/RENDER limbs exist only in L3 (writeTheRule.ts:766-818,2300). L1's protection is entirely server-side payload discipline (fullHouse.test.ts:181 BLIND COMMIT walks every pre-lock number and forbids the key substrings preview/project/estimate/expected/forecast; :223 FORBIDDEN_KEYS + forbidden curve values across every surface x phase) plus 16 constant properties in l1-tuning-harness.mjs, of which exactly ONE (P16, lines 1133/1152) renders product strings (pathDependenceCardBody, repeatSummary). Consequence: a builder can compute a projected attendance inside play/main.ts, print a target band, label CASH as 'Total Profit', or draw a fitted demand curve, and npm test stays 461/461 green and the harness still says ALL 16 PROPERTIES HOLD. OBSERVED this session: cd runtime && npm test -> exit 0, 461/461, 17.8s; node docs/gauntlet/module-2/stage0/l1-tuning-harness.mjs -> 'VERDICT: ALL 16 PROPERTIES HOLD'. MECHANISM CHECKS I RAN AGAINST THE SHIPPED BUILD (runtime/dist/modules/fullHouse.js): (1) cash-best price is $34/$48/$40/$90/$34 (New York) and $24/$36/$30/$84/$24 (Memphis) on N1-N5, at fills of 60.0-81.8% -- so the reference's 'Target: $110-$120' is not merely a leak, it is loss-making, turnout 0 and net -$520,000 (NY) / -$280,000 (MEM) on N1,N2,N3,N5. (2) fillPct = turnout/seatsOpen and seatsOpen changes with the Night-4 upper bowl: at NY N4 $84 the same 17,100 crowd renders as 86.4% (bowl closed) or 77.0% (bowl open); at $60 opening the bowl LOWERS fill 100%->93.2% while raising turnout and zeroing turnaways. Any 'of Capacity' label or fixed-bowl arena drawing is false on Night 4. (3) CurvePoint -- the only per-desk record any board frame receives -- carries no money at all (marketId, cardId, deskHandle, price, turnout, fillPct, soldOut). Per-desk cash/renewals are never on the projector; board money is per-market medians at the season-books stage. (4) The pre-lock student payload already carries the pair's own history with per-night price/turnout/fillPct/net, so a 'your own nights' chart adds no information -- but only N1 and N5 share a card, so it can never hold two comparable points before the last night. Evidence: econ-adaptation-rulings-report, -npmtest, -probe-optima, -probe-fill. TWO KID-BASELINE FINDINGS ADJUDICATED. K1 CONFIRMED, blocking for the rebuilt /play REVEAL surface: onPhaseExit force-sets twoPeaksReleased=true on leaving PLAY (fullHouse.ts:2029); boardView REVEAL then correctly gates the panel at revealStage >= NIGHT_COUNT+1 (press 6 of 7, fullHouse.ts:2522-2523); but studentView REVEAL has NO revealStage gate at all (fullHouse.ts:2246-2249) and hands every desk its own market's ticketPeakPrice, totalPeakPrice, gapDollars, gapSteps and three revenue figures the instant REVEAL opens -- the answer to the centrepiece reveal, six presses before the room sees it. Same class of defect as gate-l1-projector repair 3, surviving on the surface that repair did not touch. NOT VERIFIED: whether play/main.ts paints it today or drops the field; the payload leak is real either way and the rebuild is about to re-author that renderer. K2 CONFIRMED as model behaviour and NOT a defect, but a live false-lesson risk for the rebuilt renewals visual: OBSERVED over PRICE_GRID at RENEWALS_START, renewalDelta at $90 is -20 on N1/N2/N3/N5 in both markets but +9 (New York) and +10 (Memphis) on N4, and renewals keep GAINING up to $114 / $104 -- because renewalReferencePrice rises to $111.40 / $101.50 on a draw-97 no-TV card. The model is right and renewalRuleFor is true, but the reference price is never printed, so a pair that generalised 'high price costs renewals' from Nights 1-3 meets the opposite on Night 4.
sections.false-lesson-risks: FL-V1 BLOCKING -- 'Why didn't the highest price always win?' as a printed projector prompt. It presupposes a class result the model refutes. OBSERVED over 4,000 simulated 6-desk classes per cell: the highest-priced desk ALSO has the highest cash on Night 4 in 98.7% (timid $10-$40), 100.0% (mid $20-$60) and 31.6% (spread) of classes; on N1/N3/N5 with a timid room it still wins 37-58%. The frame would be refuted by the table printed directly above it. FL-V2 BLOCKING -- 'Your Goal: Maximize Revenue' and 'maximize revenue AND fill your arena'. Three false claims at once: the registered OBJECTIVE_COPY says the opposite ('two books... they do not add up to one number'); ticket revenue and total revenue peak at different prices (ticketPeak $42 vs totalPeak $34 at NY N1; $98 vs $90 at NY N4) which is the entire Two Peaks reveal; and revenue and fill CONFLICT -- OBSERVED, the cash-best price does NOT fill the building on 8 of 10 market-nights, the best reachable sellout is worth 34%/68%/28%/93%/34% of best cash at New York on N1-N5, and Memphis CANNOT sell out at any legal price on N1, N3 or N5. FL-V3 BLOCKING -- 'Strong Round! You're building momentum. Keep optimizing to maximize profits.' plus a trophy. Beyond D4, 'Strong' is an evaluation the model cannot make (no single objective) and it overrules the module's own teacher script, which instructs the teacher in HOOK: 'DO NOT evaluate them -- no good, no that's high. You are collecting, not marking.' 'Momentum' names a streak mechanic that does not exist; the model has two named carried channels, non-directional.
